context.purpose: Publish one bounded PNG as a WebP for web pages: encodeLossless proves every decoded RGBA sample identical (illustrations, transparent assets); encodeLossy encodes an opaque photograph-like PNG at an authored integer quality and publishes only if a fresh native decode stays inside an authored mean-RGB-error budget and byte budget. decodeToPng turns one captured static simple-format WebP back into a canonical PNG whose every sample equals a fresh trusted dwebp decode, for reports and other PNG consumers. Unsuitable for resizing, animation, metadata retention, near-lossless coding or automatic quality search.
context.assumptions: A captured local non-interlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG that is untagged or sRGB (untagged is treated as sRGB, as browsers do). Configured libwebp 1.6 cwebp and dwebp from one build; the build need not include libpng because the host supplies a canonical PAM bridge. decodeToPng needs only dwebp and a captured local .webp (one VP8L or opaque VP8 chunk).
context.constraints: At most 2048 per side, 1,048,576 pixels, 8 MiB source, 16 MiB WebP. ICC/cICP/non-sRGB gAMA-cHRM, palette, greyscale, 16-bit, interlaced, tRNS and animated PNGs are refused. Ancillary chunks are dropped. encodeLossless: fixed effort -z 6; no authored native flags. Output is not guaranteed smaller than the PNG. encodeLossy: every pixel alpha 255, integer quality 0-100 (100 is not lossless), maxMeanRGBError 0-255 required, optional maxBytes within the 16 MiB cap; fixed -m 6 -alpha_q 100; no perceptual or compression-ratio claim. decodeToPng: WebP at most 16 MiB, 2048 per side, 1,048,576 pixels; animated, VP8X (ALPH, ICC, EXIF, XMP), multi-chunk and trailing-byte files and an alpha hint that disagrees with the decoded alpha are refused (the VP8 upscaling bits are a display hint that libwebp ignores; they are accepted and the coded size is decoded); PNG output is 8-bit RGB or RGBA with only IHDR, IDAT and IEND, untagged, with host-zlib-dependent IDAT bytes; lossy input yields the libwebp decoder output, not the original picture.
context.inspection: Inspect image.webp and webp-summary.json (byte counts, dimensions, container and alpha flag - VP8L for encodeLossless, opaque VP8 for encodeLossy - pixel and hidden-RGB counts, dropped chunks, decoded RGBA SHA-256). verify needs only the trusted dwebp (SCHEMAXIS_DWEBP or a stored dwebp location; the --dwebp flag belongs to run): it re-decodes the actual published bytes; encodeLossless compares every RGBA byte with the captured PNG, encodeLossy compares every RGB sample and judges the error and byte count against the authored budgets. There is no independent host WebP decoder. For encodeLossy webp-summary.json also records the requested quality (an authored setting, not recovered from the bytes), budgets, the exact summed and mean absolute RGB error and the sample count. decodeToPng publishes image.png and webp-summary.json (source and PNG bytes/hashes, container, alpha hint, pixel and hidden-RGB counts, dwebp report, decoded RGBA SHA-256); verify re-decodes the captured WebP with dwebp and compares every sample with the PNG read by two host PNG readers.
context.recovery: INVALID_WEBP_SOURCE: absolute regular local .png. INVALID_WEBP_PNG: corrupt or outside the RGB/RGBA8 non-interlaced subset; re-export. WEBP_PIXEL_BUDGET: reduce dimensions. WEBP_COLOUR_UNSUPPORTED: export sRGB without ICC. WEBP_ANIMATION_UNSUPPORTED: export one frame. INTERPRETER_NOT_FOUND: a run needs cwebp (--webp) and dwebp (--dwebp); schemaxis verify needs only dwebp, from SCHEMAXIS_DWEBP or a stored dwebp location. UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME: use libwebp 1.6. VERIFICATION_FAILED: the published bytes, the retained evidence or its JSON types changed, or the published bytes do not decode; rerun into a fresh directory. WEBP_ALPHA_UNSUPPORTED: encodeLossy needs alpha 255 everywhere; use encodeLossless for transparency or flatten the image. DELIVERABLE_NOT_MET: the lossy file was produced but its measured mean RGB error or size exceeds the authored budget (observed.assessment has the figures); raise maxMeanRGBError/maxBytes, raise quality or use encodeLossless, then run into a fresh directory. The run is failed and unverified. INVALID_WEBP_IMAGE: the WebP is malformed, not a simple VP8L/VP8 file, or dwebp cannot decode it; re-export one static file. WEBP_FORMAT_UNSUPPORTED / WEBP_ANIMATION_UNSUPPORTED: export one static frame without ALPH, ICC, EXIF or XMP. WEBP_ALPHA_MISMATCH: the alpha hint contradicts the decoded pixels; re-export (during verification of a retained run the same contradiction is VERIFICATION_FAILED with the original fault as its cause). decodeToPng needs only dwebp (--dwebp, SCHEMAXIS_DWEBP or a stored location).

workflow.scope: A verified image artifact (PNG) can be the source; the WebP and summary publish through the normal scheduler with provenance.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure expressions and finite studies resolve before the native recipe.

lifecycle.timeout: One total deadline covers both version probes, encode, decode and the fresh verification decode. Each child CPU 120s, address space 2GiB, file output about 21MiB; standalone verify has a 120s budget. decodeToPng makes four dwebp launches in the low-level run (version and decode, then the same two in its built-in verification), six through the shared run entry point (which verifies again) and two in a stand-alone verification; no encoder launch.
lifecycle.cancellation: Shared owned process-group cancellation; serial children and a final cancellation/deadline check before publication.
lifecycle.logs: Authored/effective plan, captured PNG and byte binding, canonical PAM bridge, run readback PAM, exact launchers, input hashes, stage stdout/stderr/submissions and an independently computed summary.
lifecycle.verification: Host strict RIFF/VP8L framing and PAM reader plus a fresh trusted dwebp decode of a private copy of the actual published bytes, compared byte-for-byte with the PNG decoded by the shared bounded decoder. Not an independent decoder: dwebp is the oracle. encodeLossy: strict RIFF/VP8 framing, then a fresh trusted dwebp decode whose every RGB sample is compared with the captured PNG as an exact integer sum; the exact mean error and the byte count are judged against the authored budgets with rational arithmetic, the error budget taken as the decimal as authored. This proves pixels within budget against dwebp, not the encoder settings (quality, -m, -alpha_q) or the history of the file. decodeToPng: strict simple-format RIFF framing before any native process; fresh trusted dwebp decode of a private copy of the captured WebP; dwebp report and PAM cross-checked with the framing; every RGBA sample compared with image.png read by a strict canonical reader and the shared bounded PNG decoder. Semantic agreement with libwebp only; the source is not authenticated.

losses: Only the documented bounded PNG subset is accepted; ancillary chunks (text, EXIF, physical size) are dropped.
data.scope: Captured regular local PNG within the pixel and byte budgets.

losses: Lossless for samples, but no colour profile or metadata is carried; RGB sources gain alpha 255; file size may exceed the PNG.
encodeLossy changes RGB samples within the authored mean-error budget, requires alpha 255 everywhere and emits no alpha chunk.
data.scope: One image.webp (VP8L for encodeLossless, opaque VP8 for encodeLossy) then a text summary.

losses: Only one static simple-format VP8L or opaque VP8 file is accepted; animation, VP8X, ALPH, ICC, EXIF and XMP are refused. Lossy input decodes to the libwebp output, not the original picture.
data.scope: Captured regular local .webp within 16 MiB, 2048 per side and 1,048,576 pixels.

losses: Only IHDR, IDAT and IEND; no colour or metadata chunks; IDAT bytes depend on the host zlib while samples do not.
data.scope: One image.png then a text summary.

inspection.scope: The published WebP: lossless VP8L from encodeLossless, or opaque lossy VP8 from encodeLossy.
inspection.limits: Viewer support for WebP depends on the host browser; pixels are verified, appearance under colour management is not.

inspection.scope: JSON dimensions, sizes, hashes, pixel and hidden-RGB counts and dropped chunks.
inspection.limits: Host-authored summary recomputed during verification; not a native identify readback.

inspection.scope: For encodeLossy, quality, budgets and the measured exact RGB error and sample count.
inspection.limits: Mean absolute error against the trusted dwebp default decode; not a perceptual score and not valid for other decoders.

inspection.scope: For decodeToPng, the published canonical PNG decoded from the WebP.
inspection.limits: Samples equal a fresh dwebp decode; appearance under colour management is not verified.

authoring.reuse: Change the absolute PNG source. Retain source bytes for provenance; same-path byte changes invalidate scheduler reuse.

workflow.scope: A verified image artifact (PNG) can be the source; the WebP and summary publish through the normal scheduler with provenance.

composition.scope: Shared document references, pure expressions and finite studies resolve before the native recipe.

reusable-inputs.scope: The absolute source path and captured PNG byte digest participate in reuse identity.

source-authoring.scope: Editable JSON source with common undo and validation.

property-authoring.scope: Common pointer forms expose the source field and, for encodeLossy, quality, maxMeanRGBError and maxBytes; the contract has no other authored properties.

conversion.scope: Three named operations: encodeLossless (PNG to lossless WebP with explicit losses and native readback acceptance) and encodeLossy (opaque PNG to lossy WebP inside authored error and byte budgets, with explicit losses and native readback judgement). No other format, no near-lossless, no automatic quality search. Plus decodeToPng: one static simple-format WebP to a canonical PNG verified against a fresh dwebp decode (decoder-only).

native-inspection.scope: No interactive native inspection; the WebP and its JSON summary are ordinary publications.

mpi.scope: The recipe is serial; each native process is a single thread.

time-batches.scope: No temporal batching; common finite studies remain available.

live-editing.scope: No persistent native session; edit JSON then create a new bounded run.

native-save.scope: WebP publications are supported; there is no application session or project save.

cases.scope: Hand-built 7x5 RGBA swatch (sRGB chunk, one dropped tEXt): 18 opaque, 6 partial-alpha, 11 transparent pixels of which 7 keep non-zero RGB. Counts are literal expectations derived from the fixture design, independent of the adaptor. Native dwebp readback of every RGBA byte is the verification decision; the summary is a host record.

Hand-built 96x64 flat-colour RGBA landscape with a transparent margin carrying invisible RGB; dimensions and total pixel count are literal. Native dwebp readback of every RGBA byte decides verification.
Hand-built 5x3 RGB PNG (odd dimensions, no alpha channel): every pixel becomes alpha 255 and the WebP has no alpha flag. Native dwebp readback of every RGBA byte decides verification.

Hand-built 96x60 asymmetric opaque gradient with one dark stroke and a bright dot (RGBA, every alpha 255): 17280 RGB samples. Literal expectations: the mean absolute RGB error of cwebp -q 80 is independently expected near 2.3 (within 1 level) and inside the authored budget 3. Native dwebp readback of every RGB sample decides verification.

Hand-built 96x64 RGB colour chart of 24 flat patches with dark borders: 18432 RGB samples. Saturated edges make lossy coding less accurate (expected near 8.8 within 1 level at -q 90) and larger than the PNG; the example accepts that explicitly with maxMeanRGBError 10.

Hand-written 4x3 RGBA literal (primaries, alpha 128/64/1/254, two alpha-0 pixels keeping RGB 7,8,9 and 250,251,252) encoded by libwebp 1.6.0 cwebp -lossless -exact: 6 opaque, 4 partial-alpha, 2 transparent, 2 transparent with RGB. Counts are literal expectations independent of the adaptor; a fresh native dwebp decode of the captured WebP decides verification.
5x3 opaque lossless WebP (libwebp 1.6.0 from the committed swatch-rgb PNG): alpha hint absent, so the PNG is 8-bit RGB; 15 opaque pixels.
96x60 opaque lossy VP8 WebP (libwebp 1.6.0 cwebp -q 80 from the committed gradient): 5760 opaque pixels, RGB PNG equal to the dwebp default decode (not to the original picture).
